paragraphs.text: Some locations in this account are approximate.
The exact date of the founding of Tenochtitlan, on an island in Lake Texcoco, is unclear, but 1325 was later chosen to celebrate its anniversary.
Moctezuma I, born here in 1398, later became the fifth king of Tenochtitlan.
The Mexico Flood of 1446 is documented here.
Moctezuma II, born here in 1466, later became the ninth emperor of the Aztec Empire.
In 1473 Tenochtitlan fought the Battle of Tlatelolco against Tlatelolco, its neighbour on the island.
On 19 February 1475 an earthquake struck Tenochtitlan during the reign of Tlatoani Axayacatl.
Cuauhtémoc, born here in 1495, later became the last Aztec Emperor.
A smallpox epidemic in Tenochtitlan lasted from 1519 to 1520.
On 22 May 1520, during the Spanish conquest, the Feast of Toxcatl ended in a massacre of Mexica elites.
On 30 June 1521 the Mexica won the Battle of Colhuacatonco, regarded as their most important victory of the siege of Tenochtitlan.
Tenochtitlan fell in 1521 to the Spanish and thousands of indigenous allies, especially Tlaxcaltec warriors.
The cocoliztli epidemic of 1545 to 1548 brought high fevers and bleeding.
The Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral, dated to 1570, sits on the former Aztec sacred precinct.
The Francisco Hernández expedition ran from 1570 to 1577, and a cocoliztli epidemic lasted from 1576 to 1577.
